newsitem.title: USA: Alcoa purchase may raise competition issues.
newsitem.headline: Alcoa purchase may raise competition issues.

text.p: Alcoa's move to buy Reynolds Metals' rolling mill complex in Alabama will cut canstock competition and may raise anti-trust issues, industry analysts said.
"I wonder if it will pass the Justice Department - it's a concentration of capacity within the industry," Jim Southwood of Commodity Metals Management said.
Analysts estimated that just four companies, Alcoa, Alcan, Kaiser Aluminum and Atlantic Richfield will have 80 to 85 percent of the huge North American canstock market following Reynolds' departure.
It was widely expected that Reynolds would sell Alabama as part of a fundamental company rejig, but selling to Alcoa was unexpected, observers said.
An Alcoa spokeswoman stressed that only a letter of intent has been signed with Reynolds, and that the usual process of going through regulatory approvals would now begin.
Reynolds is expected to realize an after-tax loss of $225 to $335 million on the sale.
Reynolds shipped some 900 million pounds of aluminum products from the complex last year, and Alcoa planned to continue operating the mill to supply Reynolds with canstock on a long-term basis.
Jeremiah Sheehan, Reynolds' chairman and CEO, said the company had traditionally been a higher cost producer of cansheet and had been unable to close to gap with rivals.
But analysts said the situation provoked memories of Alcan's failed bid in 1985 to buy the Logan cansheet rolling mill from Atlantic Richfield as part of a bigger slew of assets.
U.S. Justice ruled that Alcan could only buy 40 percent of Logan to avoid overconcentration in the canstock market.
Justice's ban has since expired and some observers think that Alcoa's move may rekindle Alcan's desire to own all of Logan.
"If the Alcoa purchase goes through, then Alcan is going to take Anaconda," one industry analyst said, referring to Atlantic Richfield's 60 percent stake in Logan.
"We have said that when the time is right, we would like to own all of Logan, but we have to have a willing seller and the time has to be right," Alcan's U.S. spokesman Pat Carpenter said.
"Alcoa's move would not necessarily prompt Alcan to do anything. It's not something that's likely to happen any time soon," Carpenter added.
The North American canstock market is about 4.9 billion pounds, or 2,222,605 tonnes, by far the single largest market in the world.

Although aluminum beat off steel to capture virtually all the beverage can market, plastic is now streaking up from behind and has already began eating into aluminum's lucrative position, forcing Pechiney and others to cut canmaking capacity.
